selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What new part of creation opened to the traveler in this passage?
questions.answer: The world of animals and birds opened to him.

questions.question: What kind of realm did he enter?
questions.answer: He entered the realm of animals and birds.

questions.question: What sentence gives the main message of the creatures?
questions.answer: Their main message is that Allah alone is the true God.

questions.question: What does the passage compare each animal and bird to?
questions.answer: Each one is like a poem, a word, or a sign pointing to Allah’s mercy and greatness.

questions.question: Besides making sounds, how else do animals point to Allah?
questions.answer: Their very bodies, abilities, and movements point to Him.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention senses, powers, limbs, and tools of the body?
questions.answer: To show that every part of an animal is meaningful and carefully arranged.

questions.question: According to the first truth, what things are rejected as the cause of life?
questions.answer: Chance, blind force, and lifeless nature are rejected.

questions.question: What repeated witness comes from all living creatures in the first truth?
questions.answer: Their existence keeps pointing again and again to Allah’s living power and oneness.

questions.question: How do decoration and proportion help the traveler reach his conclusion?
questions.answer: They show careful planning and wise design.

questions.question: Why does the passage say only Allah could do this work?
questions.answer: Because making so many different creatures with wisdom and beauty is too great for anyone else.

questions.question: As the traveler continued thinking deeply, what happened before him?
questions.answer: A door opened to the animal and bird world.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the number of sounds in that world?
questions.answer: It shows that there were countless sounds and ways of expression.

questions.question: What were all the creatures saying through their condition and sounds?
questions.answer: They were saying that there is only one true God, Allah.

questions.question: What did the earth become because of their praise?
questions.answer: It became like a giant gathering place for remembering and glorifying Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the order of their parts and abilities?
questions.answer: Their parts and abilities are arranged in a balanced and disciplined way.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the structure of animal bodies?
questions.answer: It teaches that their bodies and abilities are ordered, balanced, and purposeful.

questions.question: Why can their creation not be explained by luck or lifeless matter?
questions.answer: Because their life and design are full of order, meaning, and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the first truth say about life itself?
questions.answer: It says life is given in a way that clearly shows wisdom, knowledge, and will.

questions.question: What is the center of the second truth?
questions.answer: The center is the amazing variety and beauty among living creatures.

questions.question: What does the passage say is impossible for anyone besides Allah?
questions.answer: It is impossible for anyone besides Allah to make and manage such complete and wonderful variety.

questions.question: Who is the main person observing the animal world in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the traveler who is reflecting on creation.

questions.question: What do the many voices in the passage suggest about creation?
questions.answer: They suggest that many kinds of creatures are all praising Allah in their own ways.

questions.question: How did their voices affect the picture of the earth?
questions.answer: They made the earth seem like a huge place of worship and praise.

questions.question: What is the second truth mainly about?
questions.answer: It is about the special differences, beauty, and balanced forms of living creatures.
